channel.title: Novaris Browser — updates
channel.description: Release notes for Novaris Browser, a secure browser for Windows and Linux.

item.title: 0.9.0 — Side-by-side view, a name for the new tab, background audio, Linux
item.description:
Side-by-side view. Up to four pages at once, built on the model Zen Browser uses. Drag a tab out of the list and drop it on the left or right edge of a page; the edge you are over lights up so there is no guessing. Drag the divider to change the widths, or use the arrow keys. A pane can never be dragged below seven percent of the window, because a page too narrow to read is worse than no split at all, and a fifth pane is refused rather than becoming a sliver.

Two bugs that were always there. The layout code had never been connected to the interface, so the only part of the feature that reached anyone was the sidebar app rail. Two faults were hiding inside it the whole time: it chose the page already on screen as the second pane, so a split could show the same page twice, and it did not exclude a new tab, which has nothing to place beside one.

Your name. First-run setup asks what to call you, and the new tab page greets you by it. The greeting is now the largest thing on the page, and it covers the whole day including the night the old version had no word for at all.

Audio that keeps playing. Switching tabs used to mute them. That is now a setting, on by default, so music and calls carry on while you read something else. Gaming Mode still silences everything.

First-party ad scripts. Ad code served from the site's own server is now blocked by its path as well as its host. Every rule is anchored to a path separator, because matched as plain text "ads.js" would also block downloads.js, uploads.js, leads.js and threads.js, and break download buttons across the web.

Linux. A Debian package for Ubuntu, Debian and anything else that installs .deb files, built on Linux rather than wrapped from Windows. The password vault needs a real desktop keyring and will report itself unavailable rather than fall back to an unencrypted store.

item.title: 0.8.2 — First-party ad scripts and a working filter exception
item.description:
First-party ad scripts. Ad code served from the site's own server is now blocked by its path, not just by its host. Every rule is anchored to a path separator so /js/ads.js is caught and /js/downloads.js is not.

A filter exception that works. A rule of the form ||example.com/some/path did nothing, because the parser read the path as part of the domain name. That left no way to put one file back, which is exactly what is needed when a rule goes too far.

The signing build was broken. The code-signing settings had never been validated and had been making every build fail. The hash algorithms and the timestamp server were in the wrong place, one option no longer exists, and another had been given values it does not accept.

item.title: 0.7.5 — Tab transfer, side panel, media controls, saved pages
item.description:
Tab transfer, device to device. Send a tab to another device on your local network with no server, no account, and nothing hosted anywhere. The tab is encrypted on the sending PC with AES-256-GCM before it moves, a 100-bit pairing code authorises the transfer, and only local addresses can be reached.

Side panel apps. Discord, YouTube, Spotify, Canvas, Mail and a Notes scratchpad stay open beside your tabs. Only the app you are looking at is loaded.

Media controls and picture in picture. A control bar for whatever the page is playing, with picture-in-picture that works from any site.

Saved pages. Keep an article to read offline, in a sandbox with no script execution, carrying the address and time it was taken.

Vertical tabs and workspaces. Tabs down the left, grouped, with drag to reorder, search across all open tabs, hover preview, and a right-click menu.

Privacy. Local phishing detection, the Website Trust Card, private windows, and Gaming Mode.
